# EUVD (ENISA European Vulnerability Database) API Endpoints

The European Vulnerability Database is maintained by ENISA. The European Cybersecurity Agency (ENISA) officially launched the European Union Vulnerability Database (EUVD) in April 2025, a strategic initiative designed to enhance cybersecurity resilience across the EU. Under the NIS2 Directive, ENISA was explicitly tasked with establishing a dedicated vulnerability database to support EU-wide cybersecurity efforts.

## Base URL

The base URL for the API is https://euvdservices.enisa.europa.eu/api. Official API documentation is available at `https://euvd.enisa.europa.eu/apidoc`.

## Available Endpoints

Based on multiple client library implementations, the EUVD API exposes the following GET endpoints:

| Endpoint | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `/api/lastvulnerabilities` | Show latest vulnerabilities |
| `/api/criticalvulnerabilities` | Show latest critical vulnerabilities |
| `/api/exploitedvulnerabilities` | Show latest exploited vulnerabilities |
| `/api/enisaid` | Look up an EUVD entry by its ENISA ID |
| `/api/vulnerability` | Show a specific vulnerability by ID |
| `/api/advisory` | Show advisory by ID |
| `/api/search` (also `/api/vulnerabilities`) | Query vulnerabilities with flexible filters |

All URIs are relative to https://euvdservices.enisa.europa.eu — get_advisory_by_id → GET /api/advisory (Show advisory by ID); get_by_enisa_id → GET /api/enisaid (Show EUVD by ID); get_critical_vulnerabilities → GET /api/criticalvulnerabilities; get_exploited_vulnerabilities → GET /api/exploitedvulnerabilities; get_last_vulnerabilities → GET /api/lastvulnerabilities; get_vulnerability_by_id → GET /api/vulnerability; query_vulnerabilities → GET /api/vulnerabilities.

## Example Requests

**Latest vulnerabilities:**
```bash
curl --request GET \
  --url "https://euvdservices.enisa.europa.eu/api/lastvulnerabilities" \
  --header 'accept: application/json'
```

**Look up by ENISA ID** — the `id` parameter takes the EU identifier assigned to the vulnerability (e.g., `EUVD-2025-4893`):
```bash
curl --request GET \
  --url "https://euvdservices.enisa.europa.eu/api/enisaid?id=EUVD-2024-45012" \
  --header 'accept: application/json'
```

The exploited and critical vulnerabilities endpoints have a response size limit of a maximum of 8 records.

## Search Endpoint Parameters

The `/api/search` endpoint supports flexible filtering. The search URL structure is: https://euvdservices.enisa.europa.eu/api/search?assigner=&product=&vendor=&text=&fromDate=&toDate=&fromScore=0&toScore=10&fromEpss=0&toEpss=100&exploited=false&page=0&size=10

Notable parameter details:
- For product names, spaces within the name need to be encoded as a plus sign (+).
- For vendor names, spaces within the name also need to be encoded as a plus sign (+).
- The `text` parameter searches within the CVE description.
- Score parameters range 0–10 and EPSS parameters range 0–100.

## Known API Quirks / Limitations

A couple of implementation notes worth being aware of:
- While client libraries fully implement the official EUVD API specification, the remote search functionality has been observed to have issues; certain query parameter combinations (e.g., using vendor together with toScore or fromScore) may result in some parameters being ignored or omitted by the remote service. This is a limitation of the upstream API, not the client library.
- Only integer values are allowed for fromScore and toScore (an ENISA API quirk).
- The current EUVD API presents performance constraints and limited support for high-volume or automated use, and important metadata such as CWE, CPE, and CVSS Source was not yet available at launch.

Note that a `/kev/dump` path also appears in at least one CLI client for dumping KEV (Known Exploited Vulnerabilities) entries. For authoritative and up-to-date details, always refer to the official documentation at `https://euvd.enisa.europa.eu/apidoc`.
